clue.text: Misuse of draft powers? Volunteer to help

indicators.note: misusing something puts it to a wrong purpose, so the letters that follow are put in a wrong order

parts.note: the eleven letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A grumble about a government abusing its powers of conscription, set beside a call for volunteers.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pits forced conscription against volunteering, but the 'draft powers' are just letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: To step forward is the idiom for offering yourself when someone asks who will help.

clue.text: Rid scams distributed as mobile phone hardware

indicators.note: things distributed are spread about and handed out in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Fraud-free mobile hardware being handed out, perhaps by a phone company cleaning up its act.
explanation.definitionFit: A SIM card is the small chip inserted in a mobile phone to identify the subscriber, a physical component.

clue.text: As for you, not even this style stands out

indicators.note: dropping the even-numbered letters leaves only the first, third, fifth and so on

parts.note: the odd-placed letters of these three words

explanation.surface: A personal remark: whatever others do, your look is anything but subtle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not even' reads like 'not even this', but it tells you to discard the even-placed letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An afro is a rounded hairstyle of tightly curled hair that literally stands out from the head.

clue.text: Underground press's morning reporting is some facts short

indicators.note: falling short means coming up a letter shy, so the last one is cut

parts.note: the possessive ending supplies its own letter

indicators.note: reporting means saying out loud, so the word is spelt as it is spoken

parts.note: the word as pronounced, written phonetically with a Z
data are a body of facts

explanation.surface: A dissident newspaper's morning bulletin is light on facts.
explanation.walkthrough: The S comes from the 's of press's, doing double duty. DATA loses its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Samizdat was the clandestine self-publishing of banned writing in the Soviet bloc, an underground press.

clue.text: Right-leaning politician stripped off: no love, not one

indicators.note: something off is out of order, so the remaining letters are rearranged
stripping takes off the outer layer, so the first and last letters go
saying no to something leaves it out, so that letter is taken away
not having something means it is removed from the word

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: A right-wing politician caught undressed, shown to have no love and no one.
explanation.walkthrough: Stripping the ends leaves OLITICIA; removing an O and an I leaves LITICA to rearrange. 'Right-leaning' sounds political but describes the slant of type.
explanation.definitionFit: Italic type slopes to the right, so the letters literally lean rightwards.

clue.text: Public Order Act to stop free press

indicators.note: a stopper sits inside a bottle's neck, so these letters go inside the other group
putting things in order sorts them afresh, so the following letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to rearrange for the outer part

indicators.note: letters set free can roam into any arrangement

parts.note: the letters to rearrange for the inner part

explanation.surface: A complaint that the Public Order Act is being used to silence a free press.
explanation.walkthrough: The Public Order Act is a real UK law; 'Public' is split off from it to serve as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The public, as a noun, can mean an audience: those people watching an event or show.

clue.text: Charge leaders of Albion staging social activities in lockdown

indicators.note: leaders go at the front, so the opening letter of each following word is taken

parts.words: Albion staging social activities in lockdown
parts.note: initial letters of the six words

explanation.surface: An accusation against English leaders who held social events during the Covid lockdown.
explanation.walkthrough: Albion is a poetic name for England, nodding to the lockdown party scandal.
explanation.definitionFit: To charge is to rush at in attack, which is what assailing an enemy means.

clue.text: Symbol of peace created a splash in America

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the white bird with an olive branch
second meaning: the American past tense of dive, plunging into water

explanation.walkthrough: Americans say 'he dove in' where British speakers say 'he dived in'.
explanation.definitionFit: The bird is the traditional emblem of peace, and the US past tense of dive describes hitting water with a splash.

clue.text: Boatman taken by the force as a criminal

indicators.note: being taken in by something means being held inside it

parts.note: the setter, Boatman, refers to himself as I
F is the symbol for force in physics

explanation.surface: The setter is arrested by the police and booked as a criminal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The force' looks like the police, but 'the' and 'force' supply separate pieces; Boatman is the setter's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A thief is someone who steals, one kind of lawbreaker.

clue.text: Opposed to historical oppression's initiator or starter

indicators.note: an initiator begins things, so only the first letter of the word is used

explanation.surface: Someone against historic oppression, whether its instigator or someone who began it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starter' seems to echo 'initiator', but it is the definition: the first course of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Antipasto is the Italian course of cold meats and appetisers served before the main meal.

clue.text: In images of old Briton, said to cover island

parts.note: the Picts were ancient inhabitants of northern Britain

indicators.note: covering something wraps around it, so the next letter sits inside

explanation.surface: A historian's note that an ancient Briton's depiction is said to include an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In images' looks like the start of the surface sentence, but it is the definition, an adverbial phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Pictorial means expressed through pictures, which is what 'in images' describes.

clue.text: Stop and search twice: a set-up!

indicators.note: searching means looking inside, so the answer lies within the following words

parts.note: runs across the end of the first word, the middle word and the start of the last

explanation.surface: A suspect stopped and searched twice by police protests that it is a frame-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stop and search' reads as a single police power, but 'Stop' is the definition and 'search' the instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: To cease is to come to a halt, a straightforward synonym of stop.

clue.text: See 1
Inappropriate language starts to feed braying mob outrage

indicators.note: starts are the beginnings, so the first letter of each following word is taken

parts.note: the opening letters of the two words

indicators.note: an outrage causes upheaval, so the word is thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Swearing fans the anger of a jeering crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: An F-bomb is slang for dropping the most offensive swear word, the classic example of unacceptable language.

clue.text: Corruption in the Met? I'll provide support for leader of activists always

indicators.note: corruption twists something out of its proper shape, so the letters are scrambled
in a down entry a support goes underneath, so one piece is added to the other
a leader is at the head, so the first letter of the word is used

explanation.surface: Someone vows to back campaigners against police corruption, the Met being London's police force.
explanation.walkthrough: The Met is the Metropolitan Police of London. The A from 'activists' joins the scrambled letters.
explanation.definitionFit: All the time is an everyday phrase meaning constantly, without exception.

clue.text: Decoration for Head of Police initially concealed by House

indicators.note: something concealed is tucked away inside, so this letter goes within the other word

parts.note: a chalet is a type of house

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the first letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: A medal for a police chief, kept quiet by the Houses of Parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head of Police' reads like a police chief, but 'Decoration for Head' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaplet is a wreath or garland worn on the head as an ornament.

clue.text: Burden of those who stand against us over England

parts.note: us and them: the opposing side

explanation.surface: The weight carried by England's opponents, those lined up against us.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'over' places the first piece above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: The burden of a song or argument is its main topic or recurring refrain, another sense of the central subject.

clue.text: Cycling parasite, a high-flyer

indicators.note: cycling sends something round in a loop, so the first letter moves to the end

parts.note: a louse is a parasitic insect

explanation.surface: A bike-riding freeloader who has risen to great success.
explanation.definitionFit: The ousel, or ouzel, is a blackbird-type songbird, and any bird is a crossword high-flyer.

clue.text: Article: It's the Met's Insiders!

indicators.note: insiders are at the centre, so the inner letter of each word is kept

explanation.surface: A headline exposing an inside job by London's police.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is printed in plain sight in the clue, but it is built from the middle letters of three words, not lifted.
explanation.definitionFit: The definite article is the grammatical name for this word, so it is an article.

clue.text: Speed up spending, removing new leader: reportedly you are excluded

indicators.note: removing takes something out, here a single letter
excluded means shut out, so these letters are taken away too
'leader' keeps only the first letter of 'new'
reportedly means as spoken, so letters are chosen to match the sound

parts.note: two letters that sound like the phrase, as in text-speak

explanation.surface: A plea to hurry up the budget, sacking the new boss and cutting you out.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the first N out of EXPENDITURE, then remove the U and R.
explanation.definitionFit: To expedite a task is to make it go faster, hastening its progress.

clue.text: At the right moment, after taking on uniform

indicators.note: taking something on means taking it in, so a letter goes inside

parts.note: as in 'once he had left', meaning after
U is uniform in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone arriving at just the right time, after putting on a uniform.
explanation.definitionFit: On cue means exactly when expected, like an actor entering when prompted by a line.

clue.text: Plain heartless in extremes to enact instrument

indicators.note: without a heart means the central letter is cut out
the extremes of a word are its two ends, so only those letters are kept

explanation.surface: An instruction to perform a plain piece of music with a heartless intensity.
explanation.definitionFit: A clarinet is a woodwind instrument with a single reed.

clue.text: Frustrates change of direction in glittering society

indicators.note: turning one way to the other swaps right for left, so the letter for one becomes the letter for the other

explanation.surface: A U-turn upsets the fashionable set.
explanation.walkthrough: R for right becomes L for left.
explanation.definitionFit: To blight hopes is to spoil or thwart them, which is what frustrating them does.

clue.text: One responsible for publication of Serious Disruption Order is dropped

indicators.note: disruption throws things into disorder, so these letters are jumbled
dropping something lets it fall away, so this letter is lost

parts.note: its opening letter abbreviates the word

explanation.surface: A news report that a Serious Disruption Prevention Order, a UK protest-control measure, has been dropped.
explanation.walkthrough: Serious Disruption Prevention Orders were proposed UK curbs on protesters.
explanation.definitionFit: An issuer is the party that puts out a publication, a stamp or a security.

clue.text: Wrongful arrest, one that's glaring

indicators.note: something wrongful is not right, so the letters are not in the right order

explanation.surface: Someone detained unlawfully glowers at the arresting officer.
explanation.definitionFit: A starer fixes a hard look on someone, and a glare is an angry stare.

clue.text: Carrying charge after schedule loses gagging clause?

parts.note: post is the Latin prefix meaning after

indicators.note: losing something means it is gone, so those letters are removed

parts.note: a schedule of business for a meeting
a non-disclosure agreement silences the signatory

explanation.surface: A legal note that a fee applies once a gagging clause is struck out of the timetable.
explanation.walkthrough: NDA, a non-disclosure agreement, is the 'gagging clause' taken out of AGENDA.
explanation.definitionFit: Postage is the fee paid for sending a letter or parcel, a charge for carriage.

clue.text: State finds Boatman in picket

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a picket is a pointed stake, a post
the setter, Boatman, refers to himself as I

explanation.surface: The government discovers the setter on a picket line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' looks like the government; here it is a verb. A picket is also a stake.
explanation.definitionFit: To posit is to put forward as fact, to state or assert.

clue.text: Spray operation set up against society's outsiders

indicators.note: in a down entry, setting up reads the word from the bottom upwards
outsiders are at the edges, so the first and last letters are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of society

explanation.surface: A police operation set up against members of a society.
explanation.definitionFit: A spray of flowers is a small bunch, which is what a posy is.

clue.text: Boatman, the first to defy bent copper into recollecting kidnap

parts.note: an AB, able seaman, is a sailor

indicators.note: bent back means turned round, so the letters run in the opposite direction
re-collecting means gathering up again in a new arrangement
the first means the opening letter of the word that follows

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: The setter, first to defy a corrupt policeman, recalls being kidnapped.
explanation.walkthrough: Elsewhere Boatman means I, the setter; here it is AB, a seaman. 'Bent copper' suggests a crooked cop but is a reversed chemical symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: Abduction is the act of carrying someone off by force, exactly a kidnap used as a noun.

clue.text: It's widespread in Colombia, with early signs in Central America

definitions.text: It's widespread in Colombia, with early signs in Central America

parts.note: the international country code for Colombia

indicators.note: early signs are the first marks seen, so the initials of the following words are taken

explanation.surface: A plant common in Colombia that is beginning to appear in Central America.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the definition and the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The coca shrub, source of cocaine, is grown extensively in Colombia and is starting to spread northwards.

clue.text: Take heed of national uprising to put end to injustice

indicators.note: rising up in a down entry reads the word from bottom to top
the end is the final letter of the following word, which is put last

explanation.surface: A warning to heed a national revolt aimed at ending injustice.
explanation.definitionFit: To note something is to observe and pay attention to it.

clue.text: Most passionate Saints take on players: that's tense

indicators.note: taking something on means taking it in, so these letters go between the others

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for saint, doubled for the plural
i.e. stands for id est, that is

explanation.surface: A sports report: Saints face another side, and the match is tense.
explanation.walkthrough: Southampton FC are known as the Saints, which supports the sporting picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Steamy describes erotic heat, so the steamiest scene is the most sexually charged one.

clue.text: Crimestopper gets pressure from police rule-breaker

parts.note: read as crime's topper: the letter at the top of crime
the heat is slang for police attention

explanation.surface: An informer hotline is pressured by the police.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crimestopper' is one word as printed but splits into crime + topper; Crimestoppers is a UK charity for anonymous tip-offs.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheat is someone who breaks rules dishonestly to gain an advantage.
